To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DAGLα, a key enzyme for the production of the endocannabinoid 2‐AG, is expressed in the nuclei of neurons, where it may act in concert with phosphoinositide‐specific phospholipase (PLC)‐βs.
we describe for the first time the presence of nuclear diacylglyceride lipase α (DAGL α) in rat brain cortical neuron nuclei.
we show for the first time the localization of DAGLα in nuclei of cortical neurons and provide biochemical evidence that 2‐AG is produced in nuclei of cortical cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the nuclear localization of DAGLα and PLCβ in rat brain cortical cells, and with the characterization of the mechanism for 2AG biosynthesis in nuclei from cortical neurons.
the localization and function of nuclear DAGLα, and with the role of 2‐AG produced by this enzyme within the nuclear compartment of cortical neurons.

the study of the subnuclear localization of the enzyme DAGLα, which produces the endocannabinoid 2‐AG, and its relationship with the PLCβ isoforms, which are known to be involved in 2‐AG biosynthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DAGLα is a nuclear protein, which can be involved in 2‐AG synthesis in the nuclear compartment, and this is a new and interesting aspect of the biology of this enzyme.
the nuclear DAGLα/PLCβ‐mediated biosynthesis of 2‐AG is a new and unexpected mechanism that could play a role in the regulation of gene transcription and neuronal plasticity.
DAGLα is a nuclear protein, which is not surprising, as the protein is a lipase and therefore needs to be in the nucleus to be in close proximity with its lipid substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nuclear diacylglycerols, and in particular DAGLα, are part of a mechanism that produces 2‐AG in concert with PLCβ activity.
DAGLα is a nuclear enzyme, and that it is involved in 2‐AG biosynthesis in concert with PLCβ.
nuclear DAGLα, in concert with the PLCβ family, may contribute to 2‐AG biosynthesis within the nuclear speckle compartment, which may have an impact in the nuclear regulation of gene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nuclear DAGLα may be involved in 2‐AG synthesis within neuronal nuclei, and that this process is dependent on the activation of nuclear PLCβ.
2‐AG can be produced by DAGLα in nuclear compartments, where it may act as a signaling molecule in the regulation of gene expression.
2‐AG can be produced in the nuclei from cortical neurons, and this process can be modulated by PLC‐β activity.
